title: Report exports — team review
intro: Help define the export requirements. Answer a question or suggest a change.
notice: Example only. Names are self-entered. Completed means answered, not implemented.

setup.outcome: Decide the scope of the first report download.
setup.readers: Each question names the role it is for. Alex holds the operations lead role and Jordan the access policy owner role; the questionnaire owner decides conflicts. No role needs code details.
setup.response_budget: A short choice with one example when needed. Not sure and Someone else should answer are valid replies.
setup.reviewer: Reviewing agent; questionnaire owner resumes manual review if delivery fails.
setup.decision_maker: Questionnaire owner resolves scope conflicts after checking the evidence.
setup.escalation: If evidence conflicts, present both claims to the owner. No response deadline or reminder permission is agreed.

roles.name: Operations lead
roles.knows: Runs the monthly comparison and shares reports with colleagues. Knows the reporting workflow, not the code.

roles.name: Access policy owner
roles.knows: Owns who may see which reports and the policies behind those rules. Knows the access rules, not how they are implemented.

roles.name: Report archivist
roles.knows: Retrieves earlier reports for audits or recurring tasks.

glossary.definition: The report that compares this month's figures with the previous month's.
A downloaded copy of a report that can be shared outside the application.

requirements.title: Download a report
requirements.text: Readers need a downloadable report they can share with colleagues.
requirements.details: Keep the first version focused on one report. Access rules must also apply to downloads.

questions.title: Which export format?
questions.prompt: This decides whether the first export is CSV only or also a formatted document. Is CSV enough for the monthly comparison you share?

request.recommendation: CSV only for the first version; confirm before settling scope.
request.why: A formatted document adds scope to the first version.
request.response: Choose an option, or reply Not sure or Someone else should answer. If you need a formatted document, give one example CSV cannot support and link a sample if available.

attention.next_action: The operations lead can confirm CSV or provide an example that needs another format.

questions.title: Who may download?
questions.prompt: This decides whether downloads need their own access rule. Should anyone who can view a report also be able to export it?

request.recommendation: Same as viewing: anyone who can see a report can export it.
request.why: Exported reports can be shared outside the application.
request.response: Choose an option, or reply Not sure or Someone else should answer. If stricter, name the exception and link the policy that requires it.

attention.next_action: The access policy owner can confirm the access rule or identify the policy that sets it.

requirements.title: Find previous exports
requirements.text: Readers may need to retrieve a previous export without generating it again.
requirements.details: Retention is still a question, not a delivery commitment.

questions.title: How long should exports remain?
questions.prompt: This decides whether the first version keeps earlier exports. Does any recurring task need an export more than a month old?

request.recommendation: No: defer retained exports until a recurring need appears.
request.why: Keeping exports affects storage and access policy.
request.response: Choose an option, or reply Not sure. If Yes, name the task and how old the export is, and link a policy if one applies.

attention.next_action: The questionnaire owner needs to identify who holds the report archivist role.
